target: Vocês assistiram ao jogo ontem?
english: Did you watch the game yesterday?
tip: Regular -ir past: assistir → assistiram (vocês). Third conjugation past: drop -ir, add -iram.

target: A praia estava vazia e tranquila.
english: The beach was empty and peaceful.
tip: Two adjectives: 'vazia e tranquila' – both feminine to match 'praia.' Masc. would be 'vazio e tranquilo.'

target: O trânsito está cada vez pior.
tip: 'Cada vez + comparative' means 'more and more' or 'increasingly': cada vez pior (worse and worse), cada vez melhor (better and better).

target: Ela ficou brava com a situação.
english: She got angry about the situation.
tip: 'Bravo/brava' in Brazil means angry (not brave). This is a common false friend – 'corajoso' means brave.

target: Que chato, choveu o dia inteiro.
english: How annoying, it rained all day.
tip: 'Que chato' means 'how annoying/what a bummer.' 'Chato' is one of the most useful adjectives in Brazilian Portuguese.

target: Boa sorte! Vai dar tudo certo.
english: Good luck! Everything will work out.
tip: 'Vai + dar' – the informal future, far more common in speech than the simple future (-ei, -á, -emos, -ão).

target: Eu esqueci de comprar o pão.
english: I forgot to buy the bread.
tip: Regular -er past: esquecer → esqueci (eu). 'Esquecer de' = to forget to. -er past first person: -i.

target: Ele é menos tímido do que parece.
english: He's less shy than he seems.
tip: 'Menos + adjective + do que' is how you form comparatives of inferiority: menos tímido do que = less shy than.

target: As noites de verão são quentes e agradáveis.
english: Summer nights are hot and pleasant.
tip: Time expressions use the definite article: 'às sete' (at seven), 'ao meio-dia' (at noon).

target: A minha mala é mais pesada que a sua.
english: My suitcase is heavier than yours.
tip: `-inho` softens tone: `um momentinho` (just a sec), `obrigadinho` (thanks, friendly). Not about size – about warmth.

target: Capaz! Eu nunca faria isso.
english: No way! I would never do that.
tip: 'faria' – conditional tense, expressing what would happen. Note the characteristic -ia ending added to the infinitive stem.

target: Ele é meio preguiçoso, mas muito talentoso.
english: He's a bit lazy, but very talented.
tip: 'Meio' before an adjective means 'kind of/a bit.' In informal Brazilian Portuguese, it doesn't change for gender: 'ela é meio louca' (not 'meia louca').

target: Eu morei em Salvador por dois anos.
english: I lived in Salvador for two years.
tip: Regular -ar past: morar → morei (eu). 'Por dois anos' = for two years – 'por' for duration.

target: Nós subimos a montanha em três horas.
english: We climbed the mountain in three hours.
tip: Common irregular preterites to memorize: 'fiz' (did), 'disse' (said), 'trouxe' (brought), 'soube' (knew), 'pude' (could).

target: Ele é gordo e baixo, mas muito engraçado.
english: He's fat and short, but very funny.
tip: 'Gordo e baixo' – masculine adjectives matching 'ele.' Physical descriptions use 'ser' (permanent traits).

target: A gente nadou no rio a tarde inteira.
english: We swam in the river all afternoon.
tip: Regular -er/-ir preterite: -i, -este, -eu/-iu, -emos/-imos, -eram/-iram. The 1st person -i and 3rd person -eu/-iu are most used.

target: A comida da cantina era boa e barata.
english: The cafeteria food was good and cheap.
tip: In compound tenses, 'se' attaches to the auxiliary: 'Eu me tinha preparado' (I had prepared myself).

target: Nós esperávamos bom tempo, mas nevou.
english: We were expecting good weather, but it snowed.
tip: Preterite narrates events (what happened); imperfect paints the scene (what was going on). They work as a pair.

target: Essa é a melhor pizza da cidade.
english: This is the best pizza in the city.
tip: Superlatives use 'o/a mais' + adjective or irregular forms: o melhor (the best), o pior (the worst), o maior (the biggest).

target: Ela gravou a reunião para ouvir depois.
english: She recorded the meeting to listen to later.
tip: Regular -ar past: gravar → gravou. 'Gravar' = to record. 'Para ouvir depois' = to listen later.

target: As ruas são estreitas e cheias de gente.
english: The streets are narrow and full of people.
tip: Adjectives ending in -o change to -as in feminine plural: estreito → estreitas. Adjectives ending in -e stay the same for both genders: grande → grandes.

target: A rua é escura e perigosa à noite.
english: The street is dark and dangerous at night.
tip: 'Escura e perigosa' – both adjectives in feminine to match 'rua' (street). 'À noite' = at night.

target: As meninas são tão estudiosas quanto os meninos.
english: The girls are as studious as the boys.
tip: 'Tão...quanto' = as...as (comparison of equality). 'Tão estudiosas quanto' = as studious as.

target: Ela cuidou das crianças enquanto eu trabalhei.
english: She took care of the kids while I worked.
tip: 'Ser' and 'ir' share the same preterite forms: fui, foste, foi, fomos, foram – only context tells them apart.

target: A escola era pequena, mas todo mundo se conhecia.
english: The school was small, but everyone knew each other.
tip: 'Se' can also indicate reciprocal action: 'eles se encontram' can mean 'they meet each other'.

target: O vento está forte demais para ir à praia.
english: The wind is too strong to go to the beach.
tip: 'A + o/a/os/as' contracts to 'ao/à/aos/às'. The grave accent on 'à' marks the contraction a + a (crase).

target: Bora!
tip: 'Bora' is a contraction of 'vamos embora' (let's go). It's possibly the most-used casual word in Brazilian Portuguese.

target: Que massa!
tip: Perfeito signals a change of state: 'Ele ficou triste' (He became sad) – the sadness started at that moment.

target: Que maravilha!
tip: Regular -ar verbs in perfeito: -ei, -aste (BP: -ou), -ou, -ámos, -aram. The -ei and -ou endings are the most common.

target: Tô morrendo de fome!
tip: 'Morrendo de' + noun is how Brazilians exaggerate: morrendo de fome (starving), morrendo de sono (dead tired), morrendo de rir (dying of laughter).

target: Fica pra próxima.
tip: 'Fica pra próxima' is the polite way to turn down an invitation while leaving the door open for future plans.

target: Que bacana, parabéns!
tip: 'Bacana' means nice/cool/great. It's a bit more grown-up than 'legal' and less slangy than 'massa.'

target: Eu tô nem aí.
tip: 'Tô nem aí' is a casual way to say 'I don't care.' Somewhat dismissive – use with friends, not your boss.

target: Eu tô morrendo de sono.
tip: 'morrendo' – gerund form for ongoing action. Brazilian Portuguese prefers 'estar + gerund' over European Portuguese's 'estar a + infinitive'.

target: Tamo junto!
tip: 'Tamo junto' is a contraction of 'estamos juntos.' It's a way of showing solidarity and friendship in Brazil.

target: Fica à vontade.
tip: 'Ficar à vontade' means to make yourself comfortable. Brazilians say this constantly when you visit their home or office.

target: Até que enfim!
tip: 'Até que' always triggers the subjunctive – it signals uncertainty or a condition that may not be real.

target: Que dia lindo!
tip: 'lindo' – gerund form for ongoing action. Brazilian Portuguese prefers 'estar + gerund' over European Portuguese's 'estar a + infinitive'.

target: Eita, quase caí!
tip: 'Eita' is an exclamation common in the Northeast and now used nationally. It expresses surprise or a near miss.

target: Cadê o controle remoto?
tip: 'Cadê' is a uniquely Brazilian word meaning 'where is.' It's informal and used constantly. It comes from 'que é de' (what is of).

target: Que bom que você veio!
tip: 'Que bom que' means 'how good that' or 'I'm glad that.' It's the natural way to express that you're pleased about something.

target: Vocês tomaram café da manhã?
tip: Regular -ar past: tomar → tomaram. 'Tomar café da manhã' = to have breakfast (a set expression).

target: A gente conversou até tarde.
tip: The preterite often pairs with specific time markers: 'ontem' (yesterday), 'no ano passado' (last year), 'há dois dias' (two days ago).

target: Tá na hora de ir embora.
tip: 'embora' always triggers the subjunctive – it signals uncertainty or a condition that may not be real.

target: Pois é, a vida não é fácil.
tip: 'Pois é' is a common filler/agreement expression meaning 'yeah' or 'exactly' or 'that's how it is.' Used to show empathy or agreement.

target: Oxe, como assim?
tip: 'Oxe' is an exclamation from Northeastern Brazil expressing surprise or confusion. It's spread across the whole country.

target: Tomara que dê certo.
tip: 'Tomara que' means 'I hope that' and is followed by the subjunctive. But you'll hear it so often, you'll learn it as a set phrase.

target: Vocês entenderam a explicação?
tip: Regular -er past: entender → entenderam. Plural -er past: -eram. 'A explicação' = the explanation.

target: Calma, vai dar tudo certo.
tip: 'Dar certo' is one of the most important Brazilian expressions. It means 'to work out/to go well.' 'Vai dar certo' = it'll be fine.

target: Pera aí, deixa eu pensar.
tip: 'Pera aí' is a contraction of 'espera aí' (wait there). Very common in casual speech.

target: Faz parte, vida que segue.
tip: 'Faz parte' means 'it's part of life' or 'it happens.' 'Vida que segue' = life goes on. Together, they form a very Brazilian philosophical acceptance.

target: Ela preparou um jantar especial.
tip: Regular -ar past: preparar → preparou. The -ou ending is the hallmark of third-person -ar past.

target: Ele encontrou um emprego novo.
tip: Regular -ar past: encontrar → encontrou. 'Emprego novo' – adjective after noun is the default position.

target: Ela cozinhou um prato delicioso.
tip: Regular -ar past: cozinhar → cozinhou. 'Um prato delicioso' = a delicious dish.

target: Nós compramos os ingressos online.
tip: Regular -ar past: comprar → compramos. 'Online' is used as-is in Brazilian Portuguese.

target: Ele mudou de emprego mês passado.
tip: Regular -ar past: mudar → mudou. 'Mês passado' = last month – a key time expression for past tense.

target: Eu consertei a torneira do banheiro.
tip: Regular -ar past: consertar → consertei. 'Consertar' = to fix/repair. 'Torneira' = faucet/tap.

target: A gente comeu demais no rodízio.
tip: 'Rodízio' is a Brazilian dining style where servers bring endless rounds of meat (or pizza, sushi, etc.) to your table. Very popular.

target: Ele trouxe comida para todo mundo.
tip: 'Trazer' in the past: trouxe, trouxe, trouxemos, trouxeram. The 'x' is pronounced like 'ss.'

target: Vocês descansaram no feriado?
english: Did you rest on the holiday?
tip: Regular -ar preterite endings: -ei, -aste (BP: -ou in some dialects), -ou, -ámos, -aram. The stress pattern is predictable.
